propositions: The byte-total-driven eviction backstop promised by ADR 0005 and the janitor module contract does not exist: _gc_pass reads only free disk space and entry mtime, never consulting the incrementally-maintained byte_total counter.

materialize_tickets populates the snapshot store with entries (~620 MiB each) but bypasses cache.acquire and never calls add_bytes, leaving the store's largest entries completely unaccounted in the byte_total.

The free-space watermark trigger is unreachable below 93.3% disk utilization and the promised cold-trim max-age trigger is insufficient, leaving the snapshot store with no effective size-based reclamation mechanism.

The snapshot store's real on-disk size far exceeds the reported byte_total because unaccounted materialize_tickets entries dominate the store, breaking any size-cap trigger that relies on the counter once implemented.
